newsitem.title: FRANCE: GOLF-PARNEVIK SURVIVES MONTY BLITZ AND WINS BY FIVE.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-PARNEVIK SURVIVES MONTY BLITZ AND WINS BY FIVE.

text.p: Jesper Parnevik coolly withstood an early blitz by Colin Montgomerie to win the Lancome Trophy by five strokes on Sunday when the Scot gave back all he had gained from birdies at the first five holes.
The 31-year-old Swede, who compiled a composed three-under-par 67, led by a stroke from Montgomerie at the start of the round but was two in arrears after the Scot birdied the first three holes.
But Parnevik, toughened by three years on the U.S. Tour, was unruffled and matched Montgomerie's birdies at the next two holes. Then the European number one's game began to come apart.
He bogeyed the sixth from a greenside bunker and the short seventh after hitting into water. Then after five successive pars he went completely to pieces, starting at the 13th.
Three successive bogeys against two birdies by the Swede left Montgomerie five behind and a 25-foot putt to save par at the 16th only limited the damage.
Both parred the 17th and bogeyed the last, leaving Parnevik with a 12-under-par total of 268 and Montgomerie after a one-over-par 71 on 273.
"It was a very, very good start but to be honest I didn't hit a golf shot after the fifth hole. I played remarkably badly," Montgomerie said as he tried to fathom what had happened to him.
"I left the door wide open for Jesper and he walked right through it.
"I repeat what I said before, we cannot go to Spain to defend the Ryder Cup next year without Jesper Parnevik."
The Swede is not eligible to qualify for the European team because he is not a full Tour member and unless rules are changed will have to rely on being a wild card selection.
"The start I made would have finished off most people, but not him. He played very well while I hit left and right, was in the trees, in the bushes or missing putts," Montgomerie added.
"All credit to Jesper for plugging away in determined fashion. That's what it takes."
Parnevik admitted he thought "it was all over" when Montgomerie made his first five birdies.
"He was in a league of his own. So it was a big thing for me to make birdies at the fourth and fifth to stay with him. After that I played well while Colin struggled"
Parnevik added he will probably not play any more events this year. "I need a rest. I feel my game is just about to take off."
Ross Drummond of Britain closed with a 69 to take third place, one behind Montgomerie.
Costantino Rocca of Italy and Britain's David Howell and Stuart Cage were level fourth another three shots behind and Ian Woosnam was joint seventh on two under after a final 73.

Parnevik won 108,330 pounds ($168,400) but Montgomerie's second-place cheque for 72,210 pounds ($112,300) boosted his lead at the top of the money-list as he attempts to win the European Order of Merit for a record-equalling fourth successive year.
Irishman Padraig Harrington shot a best-of-the-week 63 on the final day, chipping in from off the green three times on the back nine.
